content.title: About
content.content: Tres Leche Cake is a soft, milky dessert composed of three layers soaked in milk, cream, and caramel sauce. It is popular in Latin American cuisine and is known for its delicate texture and sweet dairy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cake is often topped with caramel drizzle and fresh berries.
Traditional recipes use three dairy products: condensed milk, evaporated milk, and heavy cream.
Some regional variations add coffee or rum for extra depth.
Tres Leche Cake is commonly served at celebrations and family gatherings.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Dairy components provide calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cream and milk contain vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The cake supplies a modest amount of protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cake contains dairy, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey should avoid this product.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Due to its sweetness, those with diabetes should limit consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the Tres Leche Cake chilled, sliced into portions. It pairs well with berries, fruit sauce, or a scoop of ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake refrigerated, covered with plastic wrap, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months.
